flags: minor: A ('still expects the shop to be rescued') is a moderately strong lure because tickets dated past the closing date could be read as hope of reprieve; the 'Somebody might come back' half and the 40-year-old tickets rule it out, but quick solvers who only use paragraph 1 may pick A
minor: stem quotes 'Somebody might come back' and locates it, which cues the drawer reveal relevant to R014-03/R014-04
R014-01.notes: Paragraph count checks out (P6 = last Saturday). Writing tickets past the closing date and keeping uncollected tickets on the chance owners return both show reluctance to let the shop's work end. B and D unsupported; A covers only part 1.

flags: minor: correct choice is the shortest, vaguest option; B and C are longer and add unsupported specifics (training as watchmaker, mother's invented task), a test-wise tell
R014-02.notes: Narrator senses the Saturdays served some other purpose for grandfather ('could not have said what the point was'). B/C invent motives; D contradicted by his expert explanations.

R014-03.notes: P2-3 introduce the 'Others' drawer and an evasive answer; P6 the narrator opens it and finds the tickets. A is a surface-level lure (labeled drawers show organization) but 'mainly serves' points to setup/payoff. C, D unsupported.

flags: minor: C (tracking down owners) is the main lure; it is unsupported but plausible-sounding, which is appropriate
R014-04.notes: Narrator hides drawer from mother and keeps it shut, protecting what the tickets mean to grandfather from being thrown out ('what would be sold and what would be thrown out'). A, B, C not supported by the text.

R014-05.notes: 'in my mother's neat capitals' (P1). Direct detail retrieval; mild possessive-inference step.

flags: minor: 'called in' applied to tickets is slightly unusual idiom; standard sense is 'demanded back/summoned' (as with a loan), i.e., the shop called the tickets in. 'Claimed by their owners' is the best fit given 'the watches returned,' but the gloss is a little loose; B 'telephoned ahead' is a literal-sense lure
R014-06.notes: Context: tickets called in and watches returned, i.e., the outstanding repairs were redeemed/collected. Only A fits; C and D off; B literal trap.

R014-07.notes: Detailed account of how, by whom, and when each part was made shows regard for history and craft. A, C, D unsupported (D is an overreach).

flags: minor: choice D's wording 'a grandchild recalling a time when the narrator was fifteen' is awkward (refers to the narrator in third person within the description of the narrator); 'when the grandchild was fifteen' or 'when he or she was fifteen' would read more cleanly
R014-08.notes: First-person 'my grandfather,' 'I was fifteen' in past tense signals a grandchild narrating retrospectively. C contradicted by first-person limited view; A, B wrong speaker.
